senses.definition: (dated) A camera: a device for taking still photographs.

quotes.text: To diagnose / Our modest pose / The Kodaks do their best
Charmian and Martin brought up the rear, armed with kodaks. We dived under the avocado trees […] and came on a spot that satisfied Martin's photographic eye.
quotes.reference: 1911 June, Jack London, chapter 17, in The Cruise of the Snark, New York, N.Y.: The Macmillan Company, →OCLC:

quotes.text: An American girl snapped her Kodak.
quotes.reference: 2011, Simon Sebag Montefiore, Jerusalem: The Biography – A History of the Middle East, page 466:

quotes.text: There were photographs everywhere: photographs framed and unframed; photographs large and photographs small, the fresh and the faded; tintypes, kodaks, “full lengths,” “cabinets,” groups—every type of photograph; […]
quotes.reference: 1913, Booth Tarkington, The Flirt, Garden City, N.Y.: Doubleday, Page & Company, →OCLC, page 70:

quotes.text: You may consult the kodaks taken at my arrest if you are curious, Archivist.
quotes.reference: 2004, David Mitchell, Cloud Atlas, London: Hodder and Stoughton, →ISBN, page 338:

quotes.text: A knot of obviously American tourists were kodaking his lodge-gates.
quotes.reference: 1917, Rudyard Kipling, The Village That Voted the Earth Was Flat:
